newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three EU states against French deficit fix.
newsitem.headline: Three EU states against French deficit fix.

text.p: German, British and Dutch officials sitting on a European statistics advisory committee argued against allowing France to use a transfer of funds from France Telecom to reduce its 1997 budget deficit, a European Commission source said on Wednesday.
But the decision on whether the plan should be allowed would be taken by the director general of the European Union's statistics office Eurostat, he said.
The spokesman for Economic and Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy also said a small minority in the committee had expressed doubts about the French plan.
He said the decision would be taken solely on technical grounds by Eurostat Director General Yves Franchet in the next few days.
"There was a small minority, two or three countries, that expressed doubts," he told reporters.
He said it was highly desirable that Eurostat came up with a decision before the Commission presented its autumn economic forecasts on November 6.

But if the decision had not been taken by then the Commission could still, by way of a footnote, take into consideration the effect of the transfer of 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom to the French government.
Commission sources estimated this amount would help reduce the French budget deficit by between 0.4 and 0.5 percent of GDP.
De Silguy's spokesman stressed the decision on the French plan would not have to be taken by the full Commission and rejected suggestions that it could be a political decision.
